aggressive_definition: Incident high-grade prostate cancer; the abstract does not provide the grade threshold.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: The association with folate varied by tumour grade (p<sub>heterogeneity</sub><0.001); higher folate concentration was associated with an elevated risk of high-grade disease (OR for the top vs bottom fifth: 2.30 [95% CI, 1.28-4.12]; p<sub>trend</sub>=0.001), with no association for low-grade disease.
study_design: Nested case-control analysis of individual participant data from six cohort studies
cohort_total_n_excerpt: A study was performed with a nested case-control design based on individual participant data from six cohort studies including 6875 cases and 8104 controls; blood collection from 1981 to 2008, and an average follow-up of 8.9 yr (standard deviation 7.3).
reason: The abstract analyzes incident prostate cancer overall and explicitly reports an incident high-grade prostate cancer association. The analysis is nested case-control rather than a full prospective cohort analysis.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Higher folate and vitamin B<sub>12</sub> concentrations were associated with a small increase in risk of PCa (ORs for the top vs bottom fifths were 1.13 [95% confidence interval (CI), 1.02-1.26], p<sub>trend</sub>=0.018, for folate and 1.12 [95% CI, 1.01-1.25], p<sub>trend</sub>=0.017, for vitamin B<sub>12</sub>), with no evidence of heterogeneity between studies.
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied folate estimate of 1.13 is explicitly for prostate cancer overall; it must not be relabeled as the separately reported high-grade estimate.
